title: The same work, made visible in the ten seconds a recruiter gives
takeaway: The README, the pins and the graph are all a recruiter sees; make those three things say something.
sources: A technical recruiter who clicks your GitHub gives it about ten seconds.
So the whole optimisation is: make those three things say something.
Almost nobody has one, which is why having a good one is disproportionately effective.
The first pin is the one that gets clicked.

before.label: Says nothing
lines: No profile README, or a wall of badges
Good work on page two behind eleven forks

after.label: Says something
lines: Three sentences on what you build, then links
Four to six finished, deployed pins, best first
Each pin has a description and a live URL
Practice repos private, old ones archived

change: The README says what you build
The first pin has the most interesting hard part
Nothing is deleted, only archived or made private
